task_brief: Day 2 of "Capstone Review, Defense, and Transition" (unit 6, grade 12) is a first concept model on independent review and critique response. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 60–90 minutes. The unit is working toward: Defend the capstone in a chosen private or public mode with complete documentation, a response to independent review, and a maintenance and transition plan. Today's work contributes to that by handling independent review and critique response at the concept model a stage, against the unit's wider topics of evidence assembly and documentation, independent review and critique response, limitations and future work, and maintenance security and sunset planning. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Study the first complete case printed in activity_setup for independent review and critique response and reduce it to a rule you could hand to someone else. Annotate the case to mark where the rule is applied and where it is only set up. Restate the rule in one sentence with no example in it, then write one fresh example of your own that obeys the rule and one near-miss that violates it. Hand-trace both and record which of your two cases the rule accepts, so the boundary of independent review and critique response is written down rather than assumed. The activity_setup block below supplies the complete central input, exact specification, execution method, test cases, debugging target, and equal-credit manual simulation; use those exact materials rather than waiting for another handout, account, service, or tool. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about independent review and critique response, and it belongs to "Capstone Review, Defense, and Transition", which also covers separate topics such as evidence assembly and documentation. Close out with this check before you stop: Explain the modelled approach to independent review and critique response in your own words and name the step most likely to go wrong. At grade 12 the bar is portfolio-quality independent work you could defend to an outside reader: intent stated, method justified, limitations named honestly, and revision traceable.

Show the process, not only the result — a trace, test log, draft trail, or commit history.

central_input.title: Inline fictional decision case for independent review and critique response
central_input.purpose: Classify and revise this case without opening a site, contacting anyone, signing in, or using real personal information.
scenario: A fictional app called Pebble Planner asks for a display nickname, exact birth date, home address, and contact list before showing a simple homework timer.
Its notice says the nickname is needed to label the timer, but gives no reason for collecting an address or contacts.
A fictional message then pressures the learner to reveal a sign-in secret immediately or lose the timer.
decision_options: B: stop, share no information, save a description of the message, and ask a trusted adult
C: invent an address but reveal a sign-in secret

expected_behavior_and_specification: The response must apply independent review and critique response to at least three labelled details from the supplied central input.
Every conclusion must identify the exact row, card, requirement, or scenario sentence that supports it.
The response must include one concrete revision or decision and explain the check that would show whether it worked.
The response must name one limitation or trade-off and explain why the available evidence does not settle it.

execution_method.primary: Paper-first method: copy the short labels, annotate them, and complete the response in a notebook or any notes app. No download, installation, account, or internet access is needed.
execution_method.local_optional: A locally available word processor, spreadsheet, drawing tool, or slide editor may be used, but no particular brand or paid feature is required.
execution_method.check_path: Use the numbered specification and the package test/check criteria as a checklist; a parent or tutor can verify the cited labels without needing subject software.

test_cases.expected: one stated check with an observable pass condition
one limitation, unknown, or trade-off stated without inventing facts

debugging_target.observed_failure: An unsupported answer names the lesson topic but cites no labelled detail and has no observable way to check the proposed change.
debugging_target.target: Replace unsupported claims with evidence-linked claims, then add one pass/fail check for the proposed revision or decision.
debugging_target.passing_change: A reader can trace every conclusion to a printed label in the central input and can perform the stated check without outside materials.

equal_credit_alternative.method: A handwritten, typed, spoken-to-a-scribe, or labelled-diagram response earns identical credit when it addresses the same specification.
steps: Label three facts from the central input.
Explain how each fact connects to independent review and critique response.
State one revision or decision and its observable pass condition.
Name one limitation or missing fact without searching for outside information.
equal_credit_alternative.evidence_to_submit: Three labelled evidence links, the revision or decision, the pass condition, and the limitation or missing fact.

test_or_check_criteria: The rule for independent review and critique response is stated in one sentence that contains no example.
One original conforming example and one original near-miss are supplied, both hand-traced.
The written boundary correctly separates the conforming case from the violating case.
No real credentials or live external systems appear anywhere in the examples.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.
Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, diagrammed, or demonstrated responses; where code is the target, accept pseudocode, block-based, or annotated-trace evidence.
Provide screen-reader-compatible editors, adjustable font and contrast, keyboard-only workflows, and an offline paper-and-trace route for every programming task.
task_accessibility_provisions: Provide a screen-reader-compatible editor, adjustable font size and contrast, and a complete keyboard-only workflow. An offline paper-and-trace route is available for every task here and is scored identically to an on-screen one.

Any model, source, or artifact under study is supplied in an accessible parallel form: text alternative or transcript, described version, and a tactile or enlarged rendering where the original is visual. The learner is never required to perceive the source in one specific channel to analyse it.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Never use or require a real password, API key, access token, account credential, private message, precise location, or identifiable image; use clearly fictional placeholder values only.
Keep all security work in sandboxed, simulated, or fictional environments; never scan, probe, exploit, or attempt access against real systems, networks, accounts, services, or people.
Use approved sites and tools; do not bypass filters, access controls, licensing, or terms of service.
Treat AI output as a draft to verify and disclose. The tutor may explain concepts, ask diagnostic questions, and help debug, but never silently completes graded project work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting independent review and critique response.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for independent review and critique response follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for independent review and critique response, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to independent review and critique response works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of independent review and critique response, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking independent review and critique response mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply independent review and critique response under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on independent review and critique response rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
